key_insight: In a young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort, Alzheimer’s and psychiatric polygenic risk showed distinct disease associations, with neither associated with measured plasma biomarkers.
clinical_relevance: Genetic risk and plasma biomarkers may provide different information, but their combined diagnostic value remains unproven.
method: Analyzed 687 European-ancestry participants: 195 controls, 283 with primary psychiatric disorders, 55 with Alzheimer’s disease and 154 with other neurodegenerative diseases.
Computed five polygenic risk scores excluding APOE; adjusted models for age, sex and APOE ε4 dose.
Assessed plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 in 332 participants.
evidence_signal: Alzheimer’s PRS was associated with Alzheimer’s disease (OR 1.69 per SD), psychiatric PRS with psychiatric disorders (OR 1.29), and adding Alzheimer’s PRS to NfL did not improve discrimination of psychiatric versus other neurodegenerative disease (AUC 0.764 versus 0.773).
watch_item: European-ancestry sampling and small diagnostic subgroups limit generalizability; larger longitudinal cohorts are needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
